To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) We developed a salience‐driven anisotropic diffusion model for image filtering, and a novel active contour weighted by extreme model for 2‐phase image segmentation; (ii) We applied the novel algorithms to third harmonic generation images to reveal key tissue components—cells, microvessles and neuropil; (iii) We validated the proposed algorithms with ground‐truth, and confirmed the results with simultaneous second harmonic generation/autofluorescence imaging.
we developed a salient‐edge‐enhancing model‐based image processing algorithm for THG brain images and applied it to reveal the morphologies of brain cells, microvessel and neuropil.
the novel proposed algorithms enable extraction of the morphologies of key brain tissue components from 3D THG images of human brain tissues.

the development and evaluation of image processing algorithms for the analysis of 3D THG images of human brain tissues, with the goal to extract morphological information about the brain tissue.

the development and validation of novel image processing algorithms for 3D THG images of human brain, and the application of these algorithms to the extraction of tissue morphologies from such images, which can report on the tissue pathological state.

the development of novel algorithms for image processing and analysis of 3D THG brain images, with the aim of extracting morphological information from them and to use it for characterizing the pathological state of human brain tissue.

we have developed novel image analysis tools, based on higher‐order statistics and active contour models, which can be used in the context of 3D THG imaging of human brain tissue, to extract morphological information from the tissue.
